content: The Roque Sáenz Peña Hospital, officially named Hospital Dr. Roque Sáenz Peña in Spanish, is a public municipal hospital located in Rosario, in the province of Santa Fe, Argentina. It functions as a secondary referral hospital, primarily serving the South and Southwest Districts of the city. The hospital is organized into three distinct areas of care: 1. Children's Health Area: This section focuses on pediatrics, neonatology, and a pediatric emergency room, providing specialized care for infants and children. 2. Adults' Area: This area offers a variety of medical specialties and includes a general emergency room to address the healthcare needs of adult patients. 3. Women's Area: This section includes a birthing center, gynecology services, and an emergency room dedicated to obstetric and gynecologic care. The hospital's labor ward manages approximately 1,800 births annually. It also runs a program aimed at promoting breastfeeding, which earned it the designation of Mother and Child-Friendly Hospital (Hospital Amigo de la Madre y el Niño) from UNICEF Argentina. The hospital's origins date back to 1921, when the decision was made to establish a healthcare and first aid facility in the southern part of Rosario. This center officially opened on August 20, 1923, at its current location. In 1933, it was named after former Argentine President Roque Sáenz Peña. In 1961, a labor ward that had been located in a separate building was integrated into the hospital.
